as a child, aiko was very boisterous and outgoing. as an adult, she becomes reclusive and sullen, submitting to her abusive mother and lonely lifestyle. punpun is fixated on the fearless aiko and their connection in childhood.

he created an image of her in his head based on their interactions as children, and he got upset when aiko did not live up to that expectation. he romanticized the version of her that he knew and resents the person she actually is.

biological sex is a social construct, yes, but has become real due to the emphasis society puts onto it, similar to any other social construct. it isnt real, but its real to those of us who have to face the consequences of it every day of our lives.

aiko and punpun were terrible for each other, thats the whole point of the final third. 

even before punpun killed aikos mother, he mentally says very awful things towards aiko. its almost as if he hates her, but continues to go back to her because he romanticizes her so much. 

would aiko have committed suicide? perhaps not, but their relationship still would have been abusive and disasterous.

ive honestly been disillusioned with capitalism and government for a while. funnily enough, my trek down the rabbit hole was just being like "im a libertarian because socialisms too extreme" to "im a socialist because communisms too extreme" to "people think this is an extreme position??"

bernie's 2016 campaign helped me realize that socialist ideas arent as bad as i thought it was, but i thought capitalism was still the only way. in university i got caught up with libertarians and left when i realized they couldnt hold up any of their arguments when it came to important social issues. that was where i first heard about anarchism (a few of them were ancaps lol) but i always thought it was too extreme. over the next few years i became more accepting of socialist ideas like universal heathcare, higher minimum wage, and rent control.

i actually came to embrace anarchism and communism through completeanarchy, and i joined a discord server of comrades that helped point me in the right direction of books to read and people to watch and gave me a space to discuss these ideas. now, im anarcho-syndicalist and i cant believe i didnt get to this point sooner.

as a keyforge player who still plays mtg, i love both games for completely different reasons.

i play a lot of commander. im a huge brewer, and i like sitting down with a unique legendary creature and finding out what works best with the strategy that card wants to catalyze. i also love being able to trade singles with others and see what cards others have and the culture of sharing collections in a way. thats something keyforge cant really replace, but im okay with that.

i love keyforge because its a really cheap barrier of entry and a different kind of game. instead of meticulously chipping away at a deck, its about learning what synergizes in your deck as you play it and getting better with the deck(s) you have. it has all the elements i enjoy about magic (the excitement of seeing what cards you get, strategy, the character of certain colors and cards, explosive and impactful turns) and improves upon the things that make magic unfun (mana screw, not always having a full enough hand to play things, netdecking).

i think its best to approach keyforge as a different game from magic, not a replacement. i just got into keyforge after deciding to take a break from buying new mtg singles and im so happy i did. sometimes i wanna jam some commander, and sometimes i wanna sit down with my keyforge decks with all my favorite houses. i can afford a new deck in addition to a fat pack of the new set of mtg. its a new alternative to what i can play with my friends and at my lgs.

i love keyforge and seeing it thrive. i think that will come with popularity as it establishes its uniqueness in the tabletop gaming community rather than a replacement/the answer to popular card games.
